summary:
Every minute counts when someone has a stroke. The faster treatment begins, the better the chances of recovery. To make sure a hospital's treatment team acts quickly and correctly in this emergency situation, some hospitals regularly practice the process in simulated scenarios, similar to a fire drill. During these exercises, the entire team, doctors, nurses, and other staff, practices together how to care for a patient with stroke symptoms as quickly and safely as possible, from arrival at the hospital to the start of treatment.

This project investigates whether introducing such regular exercises leads to stroke patients being treated more quickly. To do this, data from hospitals in northwestern Germany and Hesse are analyzed. These are data that are already routinely collected as part of legally required quality assurance measures. Treatment times in hospitals before they began these exercises are compared with treatment times after the exercises were introduced. In addition, these hospitals are compared with hospitals that do not carry out such exercises. Data from further hospitals across Germany that voluntarily report their treatment times are also included.

All data used are encoded in such a way that no one can identifiy individual patients or hospitals.

The goal of the project is to find out whether such exercises make a meaningful contribution to better care for stroke patients, so that they can be used more effectively in hospitals in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Acute ischemic stroke (ICD-10 I63)
Admission to one of the participating hospitals between January 2018 and December 2024
Admission within <24 hours after symptom onset or with unknown onset
Age >18 years (adults)
Exclusion criteria:
<18 years
